title: 0. Executive Thesis, Dual Verdict & Opportunity Matrix

epigraph.quote: A resilient franchise can still be a poor investment when a Stage 4 chart meets unquantified federal subpoenas and thin valuation upside.
epigraph.author: Executive Dossier Synthesis

web_blocks.html: What General Dynamics Does: General Dynamics (NYSE: GD) is a $92.28 billion Tier-1 aerospace and defense prime [11][13]. It runs four units: Aerospace (Gulfstream, Jet Aviation), Marine Systems (Electric Boat, Bath Iron Works, NASSCO), Combat Systems (Abrams, Stryker, LAV, munitions), and Technologies (GDIT, Mission Systems) [11][27]. In FY2025, sales hit $52,550 million (+10.1% YoY) with $5,356 million in EBIT and $3,926 million in FCF [11][33]. In 9M 2026, revenue reached $42,141 million (+10.4% YoY) with $4,407 million in EBIT, $4,827 million in FCF, and a $220.3 billion backlog [27][28].

web_blocks.html: Why Pass 2 Downgraded GD to REJECTED: Pass 1 uncovered major filing risks omitted from the prior review [27]. Note J of the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q revealed August 2026 SEC, DOJ Civil Division, and DoW OIG subpoenas into Electric Boat submarine cost records [27]. Meanwhile, 49.3% ($108.5 billion) of GD's $220.3 billion backlog is unfunded under a Continuing Resolution ending December 11, 2026 [27]. Combat Systems U.S. vehicle sales fell -$203 million in 9M after the M10 Booker exit, and Gulfstream flagged Israel mid-cabin supplier delays [27]. On cash quality, 9M EBIT absorbed $137 million in EAC uplifts while net unbilled receivables rose to $8,906 million [27]. That total includes $1.2 billion on a tracked-vehicle deal with a Note B risk warning, while Technologies carries $14.52 billion of untested goodwill [27].

Valuation, Governance & Tape Alignment: Our refreshed DCF uses an 8.8% WACC, 5.3% revenue growth, 10.7% terminal margin, and a $3.5 billion risk haircut. That model puts Base Case fair value at $355.00 (+3.95% above $341.50; expected value $336.00). At 15.97x P/FCF and 18.07x forward P/E, shares lack enough margin of safety for current risks [13]. CEO Phebe Novakovic hands over to Danny Deep on January 1, 2027, after selling 45,353 shares in November alongside GDIT leadership turnover [29][30][31]. On the chart, both facts and snapshots place GD in Stage 4 (CAP_REJECTED) with 1D RSI at 37.30 and 4H RSI at 26.55 [14]. book_paragraphs: Welcome to our refreshed institutional monograph on General Dynamics Corporation as of November 20, 2026. If you read an earlier edition of this dossier, the single most important takeaway up front is that our verdict has changed. Rather than hedging with a patient wait call, our unbiased Pass 1 forensic audit and Pass 2 valuation and tape review downgrade General Dynamics to REJECTED at TIER_0.

On the surface, General Dynamics still looks like an industrial fortress. Across Gulfstream Aerospace, Marine Systems, Combat Systems, and Technologies, the company generated $52.55 billion in FY2025 revenue and $42.14 billion through the first nine months of 2026, backed by a record $220.3 billion backlog and 13.22 percent return on invested capital. That underlying franchise strength is why Pass 1 kept our price-blind business quality at COMPOUNDER_PASS with a PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI health flag.

Yet Pass 1's deep-dive into the Q3 2026 Form 10-Q uncovered six material risks that change the investment math. Note J disclosed August 2026 subpoenas from the SEC, the DOJ Civil Division, and the DoW Office of Inspector General examining Electric Boat's submarine cost accounting and financial disclosures. Nearly half of GD's headline backlog—$108.5 billion—remains unfunded while federal spending relies on a Continuing Resolution expiring December 11, 2026.

At the same time, Marine Systems' 7.9 percent Q3 margin benefited from a Virginia Block IV completion adjustment across a 42.9 percent fixed-price nine-month revenue base, consolidated nine-month profits included $137 million of EAC catch-up uplifts, and net unbilled receivables expanded to $8,906 million with a $1.2 billion variable-consideration warning on an international tracked-vehicle contract.

Segment and leadership shifts compound those balance-sheet watchpoints. Combat Systems lost $203 million in nine-month U.S. military vehicle revenue after the M10 Booker termination, Gulfstream flagged mid-cabin airframe supplier delays in Israel alongside a G400 certification slip, Technologies holds $14.52 billion of untested goodwill, and CEO Phebe Novakovic sold 45,353 net shares in November ahead of her January 1, 2027 handover to Danny Deep.

When we rebuild our valuation from scratch at the November 20 close of $341.50 without anchoring to prior targets, Base Case intrinsic value drops to $355.00 per share—just 3.95 percent above the market price—while our probability-weighted expected value sits at $336.00. Even at the $339.20 top of the technical band against a $315.00 structural floor, reward-to-risk is just 0.65-to-1, far below our 1.50-to-1 hurdle.

The chart and portfolio liquidity seal the call. Both our facts ledger and live snapshot agree that GD is trapped in a Stan Weinstein Stage 4 downtrend below its $358.35 30-week moving average, with 4-hour RSI at 26.55 and no upward turn, inside an S&P 500 Downtrend carrying 10 distribution days. Because GD is NOT_HELD across Schwab and Robinhood and total US portfolio cash is just $2,540.35 (3.38 percent of net worth) against a 22.0 percent Downtrend floor, 100 percent of marginal capital stays in Cash.
Walk through the ten chapters ahead to examine every footnote, reverse DCF assumption, peer multiple, and multi-timeframe chart level behind that disciplined pass.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION
book_callouts.text: Good research updates its verdict when new facts arrive. Submarine subpoenas, 49.3% unfunded backlog, $8.91 billion in unbilled receivables, a $355 Base fair value, and a confirmed Stage 4 tape turn a borderline watchlist idea into a clear REJECTED call.
